title: feat(spec,lint): a notify recipient form `{ emailField }` — the address in an email-typed field of the triggering record
body:
Fixes #25610

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: added
Ruling-ref: 6377731715

The protocol half of #25571. Ruling 6377731715 on #25496 (batch #388 item 4, letter B for #25444), agreeing with 6377842908 on this row: 「收件人只能来自记录的 email 类型字段，⛔ 不接受自由文本或表达式拼出的地址；按地址限速，记消息日志」. The runtime half (resolving the field to an address, template render, outbound mail configuration, per-address rate limit, guest-input sanitising, the messaging-log entry) is #25571 and is not in this PR.

## What changes

**`@objectstack/spec` — the form.** `notify.recipients` takes a fourth union arm, `NotifyEmailFieldRecipientSchema` (exported, with its type `NotifyEmailFieldRecipient`): `{ emailField: 'applicant_email' }`, a closed object whose one key holds a field's machine name (`FieldSchema.name` grammar). A string can never parse as it (a string stays a user id or audience selector), and an envelope can never parse as it (an envelope stays a CEL value; `emailField` holding an envelope is refused). Two more constraints ride `NotifyConfigSchema`:

- it is the WHOLE `recipients` value, never a list entry (refused with its own sentence);
- the node names `email` as its only channel (`channels: 'email'` or `['email']`); no `channels`, or any other channel, is refused at `channels`. An address no user holds has no inbox.

**`@objectstack/lint` — the publish-time refusal.** `validateNotifyEmailFieldRecipients`, a reference-integrity suite member (so `os validate`, `os lint`, `os build` and the runtime publish door for a `flow` write all run it), resolves the named field against the trigger object's declared fields. Three gating verdicts:

| rule id | when |
|---|---|
| `notify-email-field-unknown` | the trigger object declares no such field |
| `notify-email-field-not-email` | the field is declared and is not `email`-typed |
| `notify-email-field-no-trigger-record` | the flow hands its run no record of a known object: a schedule, an inbound api call, a record trigger naming no object, or no record trigger at all |

The triggering record's object is the start node's `objectName` for a record trigger and `timeRelative.object` for a time-relative sweep. A trigger object this stack does not declare (another package's, `sys_*`) or one declaring no fields is skipped, like the rest of the field-existence family.

## Measured premise (origin/main 481ac62116)

- `NotifyRecipientsSlotSchema` (was `:292`) types `recipients` (was `:547`) as string | list | CEL envelope. Holds.
- PM assumption "a liveness-ledger row in `packages/spec/liveness/flow.json`": **disproved.** `FlowNodeSchema.config` is `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())` (`flow.zod.ts:630`), and `flow.json` holds `nodes.config` as a single `live` leaf with no children. No ledger row can name a notify config key, let alone one union arm of its value. So no ledger row was added and the gate was not touched. Instead, the `recipients` `.describe()` (what authors read in Studio and the reference docs) and the changeset both say delivery is not live until the messaging half lands.
- What a run does with the form today (read, not executed): `notify-node.ts#resolveRecipients` hands a non-envelope object through `resolveValueSlot` unchanged and fails the node with "evaluated to a map, not a recipient". So the form fails at the node, loudly. It is never silently dropped.

## Tests

The full package suites ran on `8934b74b`, before the one `origin/main` merge (`8040d181`, which brought #25617). On the final head `433f7f2005` (merge plus the ADR-0122 `NotifyEmailFieldRecipientParsed` alias) I re-ran `tsc --noEmit` for spec, the four touched test files (139 tests), `check:generated` (all 14 up to date) and every derived gate (below).

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec test`: 715 files / 21704 tests passed (1 todo). Includes the new `notify-email-field-recipient.test.ts` (17 tests) and the updated JSON-Schema arm pin in `io-node-config.test.ts`.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint test`: 159 files / 7243 passed, 5 skipped. Includes the new `validate-notify-email-field-recipients.test.ts` (11 tests) and the suite's member list and every-member-fires pins.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint typecheck`: green.
- Consumer: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-automation typecheck` and `test` (199 files / 2628 tests) green. It parses `NotifyConfigSchema` at execute time.
- Ablations (each mutation went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, which checks the anchor hit and that restore left `git diff HEAD` empty):
  - lint `if (type !== EMAIL_FIELD_TYPE)` to `if (false)`: 3 tests red (not-email, nested region, publish door). Restored, blob == HEAD.
  - spec `if (channels.length !== 1 || channels[0] !== 'email')` to `if (false)`: 4 tests red. Restored, blob == HEAD.

## Gates

Derived with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` on `433f7f2005`: **113 commands, every one exit 0**. Each exit code was captured to a file before any pipe. `--ran` reconciliation: "113 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 113 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero — all 113 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3)".

- The first pass, on `8040d181`, had three prerequisite refusals (exit 3): `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` (shallow clone), `check:skill-examples` (client packages not built) and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (no dist). It also had one real finding: `check:spec-parsed-alias` (ADR-0122: a bare alias read `z.infer`). I fixed the finding in `2a26b7e90b`, unshallowed the clone, built `client` and `client-react`, and re-ran the whole list. All green.
- Local-only `check:dev-prereqs`: exit 0.
- `test:repo`, dogfood and the full farm are CI's. There is no `!` in the title and no `(narrowing)` arm, so no dogfood battery is owed.

## Acceptance notes

- **Decided in this PR, beyond the ruling's words (reviewer, please confirm):** (1) the form is the whole `recipients` value, never a list entry; (2) the node must name `email` as its only channel. Both are narrow on purpose. Widening either later is non-breaking. Narrowing after release would be breaking.
- **Not judged:** a trigger object another package declares. The runtime half resolves the field against the live object.
- **No ADR edit.** ADR-0012 already maps a resolved recipient to an email address on the email channel. This PR stays off governed surfaces.
- **Docs:** only the auto-generated reference changed. The hand-written `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` recipients paragraph is not touched, so it does not advertise a form the runtime does not deliver yet. It belongs with #25571.
- **Existing literal-address path (observation, not changed here):** today a plain string recipient that looks like an email, or a CEL envelope that evaluates to one, already reaches `service-messaging`'s email channel as a literal address (`email-channel.ts#resolveRecipient`, `EMAIL_SHAPE`). The `recipients` docblock lists "an email address" as an audience selector. The ruling's 「⛔ 不接受自由文本或表达式拼出的地址」 reads against that path too. Narrowing it is a breaking change outside this card. Reported to the seat in the dev report.
